key_insight: This paper introduces a way for multiple agents to learn coordinated preferences, so they can make complementary trade-offs across conflicting objectives instead of optimizing independently. The result is more coherent team behavior in multi-objective multi-agent reinforcement learning.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of cooperative multi-objective decision-making where conflicts arise both across objectives and across agents with different observations, roles, and contributions.
method: Proposes Preference Coordinated Multi-agent Policy Optimization (PCMA) to learn agent-specific preferences in a coordinated way.
Uses coordinated preference learning to align trade-offs among agents while preserving each agent's role and local perspective.
Provides a theoretical formulation for cooperative multi-objective optimization in multi-agent settings.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a practical framework for training teams of agents to balance multiple goals without forcing a one-size-fits-all policy. It can improve performance in complex cooperative tasks where different agents need different trade-offs.
visual_elements: A multi-agent diagram showing agents with different roles and observation spaces feeding into a shared coordination module.
A preference trade-off plot illustrating how different agents balance conflicting objectives.
A pipeline chart of PCMA: local preferences -> coordination -> policy optimization -> team behavior.
An icon-based comparison between independent optimization and coordinated preference learning.
paper_title: Learning Coordinated Preference for Multi-Objective Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
paper_authors: Pengxin Wang, Lihao Guo, Yi Xie, Bo Liu, Siyang Cao
